description:
FOUND s499d (Opus prose agent, 2026-09-27) while re-verifying docs/pcl-commands.md; confirmed by Fable: `pcl -e "print qq{@INC[0,1]}"` prints `/tmp .` while perl 5.40.3`s @INC has no "." (removed in 5.26 for security) and never the script`s directory (that is FindBin / -I / `use lib`).

WHERE: pl2cl`s emitted preamble ";; Initialize @INC from Perl" (~lines 661-690): it pushes the source file`s directory, then ".", then PCL`s lib/, then perl`s own @INC entries.  Not ruled anywhere (grep DECIDED / not-supported for @INC: nothing on this).

WHY IT MATTERS: (1) a program with a stray Foo.pm in its cwd loads it under PCL and dies "Can`t locate Foo.pm" under perl -- PCL lives where perl dies, silently, and the module it loads is not the one the author meant; (2) `pcl -e` puts the RUNNER`S temp directory first, so anything another user drops in /tmp shadows a core module for every -e program; (3) `perl -I.` / `use lib "."` programs cannot be told apart from ones that rely on the accident.

FIX SHAPE: drop both entries from the preamble; anything in the tree that relied on them (tests that `require` a sibling file without `use lib`/FindBin, `tools/pclperl-for-tests`, the sweep`s harness which already gets its own -I) shows up as a NEW sweep/companion/gate failure and is fixed at the call site the way perl code does it (`use lib`, `FindBin`, `-I`).  perl-tests/t/test.pl sets @INC itself.  A `PERL5LIB`/-I mechanism must keep working (pl2cl:688 pushes perl`s entries -- keep those).
BAR: the emission preamble changes (gen bump; corpus-diff = every file, one class); gate; FULL sweep; companion --quick (the harness`s -I paths are the risk); `tools/everyday-smoke.pl` NEW 0 (an everyday program that requires a sibling module would be the honest mover -- name it); tools/t/install-pcl.t (the installed tree`s lib/ must still be found -- it is pushed separately at pl2cl:678).
PRIORITY: medium (security-shaped divergence; ordinary programs are unaffected unless a stray .pm exists).

=== DONE (s499g) ===
The preamble pushes PCL's lib/ then the transpiling perl's /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3 /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3 (which carries -I and PERL5LIB) -- no ".", no script directory; pcl's -M branch no longer adds the script dir with -I and the script-cache seed list lost both too.  Runtime: `require "x.pl"` / `do "x.pl"` search /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3 /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3 only; ./ and ../ (and absolute) paths are explicit (%p-explicit-path-p, perl's path_is_searchable).  FOUND AND FIXED on the way: `use lib EXPR` of any non-literal shape (`use lib $FindBin::Bin`) was SILENTLY DROPPED -- the script-dir accident hid it for the FindBin idiom; `use lib qw(a b)` put b first.  Guards Pl/t/use-require-01.t (7 rows fail on a 7b74e399 extraction).  Bars: corpus-diff = every file, ONE class (the "." line); emission-ab lib+shapes 30 DIFF preamble-only RCDIFF 0; gate 269/9016 PASS; sweep TOTAL 18714 (+0) GATE clean; install-pcl.t PASS.  Contract: ir-spec Â§9.  Residue filed: #2460 (-M temp copy $0/FindBin), #2461 (-e $0), #2462 (/home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3 /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3 order / tree root), #2464 (use lib dedupe).
subject: @INC under PCL starts with the SCRIPT`S DIRECTORY and "." (pl2cl preamble lines ~661-690) where perl 5.26+ has neither -- `require Foo` finds a Foo.pm beside the script or in the cwd that perl would refuse (silent divergence, and for `pcl -e` the "script directory" is the temp dir the program was written to)
